executiveSummary: GM1742's 2025 identity, 38,836-person municipality control, 46 neighbourhoods in ten districts, two BAG places, ten BRT settlements, eight NWB boundary links, Rijssen and Holten stations and 152 scheduled-transit stop areas are coherent, and the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service model contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns a fixed 0.914835 m direct flood value from T+12 through T+72, rising from 9,572 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 to 10,768 at T+72, without selecting a Regge, Schipbeek, Soestwetering, rainfall, sewer, groundwater, control or recession event; this conflicts with the adopted Twente profile's limited, local, short-lived river-overflow mechanism. Eight nonzero single-hazard presets reuse exactly the same T+24 top-five neighbourhood order. A controlled source at [6.41620728068325, 52.29244865158755], inside an official BRT 2024 mixed-forest polygon and BU17420303 De Holterberg, produces direct fire 0.616925 while its containing neighbourhood ranks thirteenth of 46. The municipal water programme documents infiltration, wadis, blue arteries, separated rainwater, a 70 mm/hour new-system design goal and known heavy-rain limits at the Maxima, Plompgraven and HW Jansen rail underpasses, but none drives the pluvial footprint or station/access state. Public water, grid, antenna, education, acute-care, road and transit sources are valuable context, not proof of live topology, occupancy, capacity, outage or recovery. Current road and drought notices require issue/valid/expiry handling; absence of a matching record is Unknown, and plans or registers are never an all-clear.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1742 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, BAG-place and BRT-settlement context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1742 as Rijssen-Holten in Overijssel and reports 38,836 residents, density 413/km², 20% aged 65 or older and 3,923 one-person households; the generated centre [6.440226361314598, 52.28946829172907] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

All 46 neighbourhood rows in ten districts expose the 36-field contract. Their independently rounded population values sum to 38,825, eleven below the municipality control (-0.028%); households sum to 14,795 and age-65-plus rows to 7,760. Deterministic local allocation reconciles to 38,836 without rewriting the observations.

BAG supplies two active woonplaatsen, Rijssen and Holten, with label points inside the generalized boundary. BRT TOP10NL supplies ten settlement labels: three woonkernen and seven buurtschappen, including Dijkerhoek, Espelo, Borkeld and Holterberg. Dataset-purpose differences do not prove omitted people or operational facilities.

Core population fields cover 46/46 rows. Home value and several housing/benefit fields cover 41/46, cars per household 40/46, doctor and supermarket distance and density 44/46, while district heat and public charging cover 0/46. Publisher null, suppression, out-of-scope and official zero remain distinct; annual residents are not incident-time occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted Regionaal Risicoprofiel Twente 2025
supports: The profile describes Twente as relatively high, without dike rings or primary defences. The Regge and Dinkel can cause locally limited, short-lived flooding during heavy or prolonged rain, while high sandy ground makes rainfall dependence and drought more material. Possible indirect effects of an IJssel flood were still being assessed.

For Rijssen-Holten it identifies a railway through both Rijssen and Holten carrying dangerous goods through partly built-up areas, and dry nature in the southern municipality that is susceptible to nature fire during prolonged drought. Regionally the A1/A35 corridor and international railway are determining logistical infrastructure.

The nature-fire assessment names campsites, recreation grounds, day visitors, constrained paths, limited firefighting water, time to build large water transport, escape routes and self-reliance as impact factors. It therefore supports dynamic visitor/access/water requirements, not a uniform resident-only footprint or a guaranteed suppression curve.

The profile covers extreme rain hindering roads and responders, power interruption, drinking-water quality/quantity, telecom/ICT and cyber dependencies. It is adopted planning and risk-selection evidence, not a live incident, probability, closure, dispatch, capacity, operator state or restoration promise.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Adopted Visie en Programma Water en Riolering 2023–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Council decision 2023-0083, adopted 21 December 2023; programme horizon 2023–2027
supports: The adopted programme distinguishes municipal wastewater, rainwater and groundwater duties and the surface-water role. It records extensive infiltration facilities, wadis, blue arteries, settlement tanks, disconnection of paved area, separately collected rainwater and retention ponds.

New systems are to be designed for a 70 mm rainfall event in one hour, using use-hold-store-discharge and continued separation of clean rainwater from wastewater. The goal and planned kilometre-per-year adaptation rate through the programme period are design/policy evidence, not achieved event performance.

The municipality states that drainage at the Maxima, Plompgraven and HW Jansen rail underpasses cannot process heavy showers; the tunnels fill, seriously hinder north-south traffic in Rijssen and make the station platform inaccessible. Planned improvements were complex and their completion, capacity and incident state are not established by the programme.

Vechtstromen, Rijn en IJssel and Drents Overijsselse Delta participated in the programme. The programme also calls for groundwater monitoring, drainage inspection and joint wastewater/surface-water work, demonstrating a multi-owner chain rather than one generic water/drainage service.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Current drought, water-shortage, high-sand and Regge operating context
evidenceSources.edition: Live public context inspected 3 September 2026; page updates include July–August 2026 drought notices
supports: Vechtstromen calls the July/August 2026 drought exceptional and records an actual national water shortage; low water and heat can degrade water quality, while the board raises weirs, supplies water where possible and may restrict abstraction. These statements are time-sensitive regional context, not a GM1742 service state.

The board explains that parts of its high sandy area, often tens of metres above sea level, cannot readily receive lake or river water and depend on rainfall. Groundwater recharge is not one-to-one with rain because water evaporates, is taken up, drains through streams or sewer, or infiltrates.

Regge levels respond to upstream inflow, weirs, vegetation and intake from the Twentekanaal; published current or historic Regge values are point/time observations, not a municipal flood surface, defence state, tunnel depth or 72-hour hydrograph.

A public page inspected at one time cannot be projected through T+72. Each restriction, level or drought statement needs observed/issued time, spatial scope, status and expiry; a lifted restriction or absent item must not be recast as permanent water availability or safety.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — BRT TOP10NL terrain point query for controlled Holterberg fire
evidenceSources.edition: BRT terrain feature source actuality 2024-01-01, registered 2025-09-01; CC BY 4.0
supports: A reproducible point-in-polygon check places [6.41620728068325, 52.29244865158755] inside BRT feature 48316e9d-5574-5b81-aaf9-91dcbc946ad3, type 'bos: gemengd bos', and inside official neighbourhood BU17420303 De Holterberg.

BRT land use establishes a controlled combustible-land-cover location for allocation testing. It does not establish current fuel load or moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind, smoke plume, visitors, escape routes, suppression water, crew state or damage.

Source actuality and registration time are different from the 2026 exercise reference date. A future adapter must retain source date, geometry, class, licence, coverage and NoData and combine it only with incident-valid fire and weather inputs.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — A1, rail, scheduled transit and expiry-aware current municipal road-work context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots 30–31 August 2026; municipal notice published 28 August 2026 and valid 2–4 September 2026
supports: The generated graph has eight domestic boundary links to five neighbours: three non-additive A1 edges, two N332 edges, and N344, N752 and N755. Nominal 260/150 capacities are scenario units; boundary links do not encode internal junctions, rail underpasses, local detours or emergency destinations.

ProRail geometry/registers place Rijssen and Holten stations inside GM1742 and OVapi geometry yields 152 stop areas by boundary containment. Static geometry and a feed valid 30 August–12 December 2026 do not prove running services, passenger counts, accessibility, freight, platform access, disruption or recovery.

The municipality announced Nijverheidsstraat closed from 2 September 2026 06:00 until an expected reopening on 4 September 2026 07:00 with a defined detour; the connected Morsweg/Spoelerstraat-Noordermorssingel works ran through 4 September. At the audit reference time this is relevant current context but must expire or update rather than persist.

The national NDW snapshot is context-only and does not make current municipal notices causal. No matching live feed item is never proof that A1, local roads, rail, tunnels or transit are open; an explicit issue/valid/expiry and route-geometry adapter is required.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards; Netbeheer Nederland; Enexis; RDI; DUO; RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, electricity planning/live page, antennas, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; contributor dates vary; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Full-boundary containment assigns 82 HWH records to GM1742: four sewer pumps, six surface-water pumps, two wastewater treatments and 70 weirs. Managers are Vechtstromen 37, Rijn en IJssel 19, Drents Overijsselse Delta 20, generic Waterschap one and Unknown five; 74 records lack capacity. Registered points do not establish connectivity, comparable throughput, controls, power, current state or recovery.

One postcode-level NBNL planning sample identifies Enexis area RS Rijssen with 43.6 MW existing withdrawal/injection, 18.4 MW/70 requests queued for withdrawal, 16.1 MW/60 requests queued for injection, TenneT classes 3/3 and thirteen projects. Enexis separately reports congestion planning and a live Holten interruption page; planning values are not load/outage, and a live 'none known' statement is valid only for its place, scope and access time.

The context assigns 74 RDI antenna records (37 mobile, 21 fixed link, fifteen amateur and one broadcast) and 30 DUO education locations. Points do not establish coverage, backhaul, power/backup, occupancy, shelter role, accessibility, capacity, staffing, supplies or restoration.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 assigns zero questionnaire respondent locations inside GM1742, and local KNMI station, KNMI seismic-origin, RIVM PM2.5, RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast matches are also zero. Each is no record in a bounded scope, not zero care, weather, smoke, seismic hazard or water; all public-context layers remain non-causal.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Adopted Zorgrisicoprofiel Twente 2025 and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Care-risk profile 2025, adopted 23 April 2026; RIVM questionnaire version 1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The profile identifies two hospital organisations with locations in Enschede, Almelo, Hengelo and Oldenzaal, while many care partners work in rural areas. GM1742 therefore depends on cross-municipal acute-care access even though the RIVM covered dataset has no SEH point inside its boundary.

Older independently living people, people with disabilities and home medical-device users are especially vulnerable to loss of power, water or internet. Aggregate age and household counts do not identify individuals, current care dependencies or who needs outreach.

The profile says not all care institutions have emergency power and existing systems are not always reliable; diesel and food delivery, alternative communications, vulnerable-client inventories, evacuation, re-placement, patient registration, staffing and aftercare require explicit preparation.

This is governance and preparedness evidence. It does not establish event-time hospital acceptance, beds, staffing, diversion, ambulance travel, care-home occupancy, backup endurance, fuel or completed first-72-hour actions.

identity.summary: Official 2025 identity, centre, province, safety region and headline controls agree.
notes: Manifest, generated context and model uniquely identify GM1742 as Rijssen-Holten in Overijssel and assign Veiligheidsregio Twente.
BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition are 2025. Current 2026 notices, source-feature dates, policy horizons and the synthetic exercise clock retain separate temporal semantics.
The municipality centre and both active BAG woonplaats label points lie inside the generalized boundary; no code, name, province, safety-region or centre-containment contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but three catchments, high-sand groundwater, rail underpasses and combustible Holterberg require mechanism-specific surfaces.
notes: The municipality spans urban Rijssen, Holten, dispersed rural settlements, Regge-side low ground and high dry Holterberg/Borkeld terrain. One municipality-centre distance cannot represent those regimes.

The adopted sources distinguish locally limited Regge overflow, rain-dependent high sand, groundwater/infiltration, sewer and surface-water pathways, with Vechtstromen, Rijn en IJssel and Drents Overijsselse Delta roles.
Generalized CBS areas, BAG/BRT labels, BRT land cover and asset points have different purposes, dates and licences. None by itself is a flood, drainage, smoke, access or service footprint.

demography.summary: Headline demography agrees and rounded neighbourhood populations reconcile within CBS publication semantics.
notes: Generated and official population is 38,836, density 413/km², age65Pct 20 and one-person households 3,923.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 38,825 (-11, -0.028%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 38,836. Published households sum to 14,795 and age65+ rows to 7,760.

The largest rows are Veeneslagen West 3,525, Plan Zuid 3,425, Veeneslagen Oost 3,210, Braakmanslanden noordoost 2,065 and De Kol en Noordenberg 2,025. Counts do not establish homebound status, disability, visitors, commuters or household supplies.

regionalDetail.summary: All 46 neighbourhoods load, but bounded missingness and non-causal public infrastructure context require persistent Unknown/NoData semantics.
notes: All rows provide core population fields. District heat and public charging are missing in 46/46, home/housing/benefit values in five, cars per household in six, and density/doctor/supermarket distance in two. Null is not zero.

The 82 water-control/wastewater points confirm multiple owners and asset classes, but 74 lack capacity and the eight present values lack a common unit/topology contract. 'Realised' or registered is not live operation.

One grid-planning sample, antenna and education registers, and zero local acute-care/observation matches remain context-only. Their coverage, date and affectsSimulation=false status must stay visible.

settlements.summary: Rijssen and Holten BAG places plus ten BRT settlement labels are spatially coherent; transient and operational roles remain Unknown.
notes: The two BAG places are active and inside the boundary; BRT adds Beuseberg, Borkeld, Dijkerhoek, Espelo, Holterbroek, Lichtenberg, Look and Neerdorp alongside Holten and Rijssen.
Three BRT woonkernen and seven buurtschappen are cartographic settlement classes, not independent population controls or emergency zones.
Labels and scheduled stops do not establish isolated households, event occupancy, fire visitors, evacuation demand, reception points, care, supplies or route access.

transport.summary: Road, rail and transit registers are reproducible, but internal rail-underpass, A1/rail, current restriction and external-destination dependencies are absent from the causal graph.
notes: Eight logical NWB edges connect Wierden, Hof van Twente, Lochem, Deventer and Raalte over A1, N332, N344, N752 and N755. Shared A1 provenance is non-additive and 260/150 capacities are scenario units.

Rijssen and Holten stations and 152 stop areas are static/scheduled context. The graph cannot express dangerous-goods rail, internal station access, Maxima/Plompgraven/HW Jansen underpass flooding, rail-road common cause, A1 junction state or acute-care travel.

A valid municipal notice covered a local closure at the audit reference time, but it is not a model state. Current restrictions must be location/time matched and expired; no national feed match is Unknown, never all-open.

emergencyContext.summary: Official risk and preparedness roles exist, but the simulator has no auditable local action, resource, occupancy or decision state for T+0–72.
notes: A usable run needs time/authority/status/resource records for warning and communication; tunnel, road and rail control; fire perimeter, visitor clearance and water supply; homebound/care outreach; medical transfer; reception; temporary drinking water; fuel, food and medicines; utility repair and mutual aid.

At T+0–6 validate event origin/forcing and activate accountable owners; by T+6–24 record tunnel/route inspections, fire and water-control actions, visitor/care accounting and external-care acceptance; by T+24–72 tie reopening/restoration to inspections, resources and completed actions.

Thirty education records are not shelters, zero internal RIVM acute-care respondents is not zero care, and annual visitor/resident values are not current occupancy. External destinations, staffing, backup, stocks and accessible routes remain Unknown.
Operator topology, control, crews and inventories may be unavailable or sensitive. Use authorised aggregates or visibly synthetic assumptions, never invented precision.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets return complete finite deterministic outputs at six checkpoints for eight services; local realism failures are separate.
notes: The mandatory and focused gates ran severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

At T+24 severity / post-network pressure / affected resident-equivalent / cumulative event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.096873 / 0.254840 / 6,283 / 138,693.391; pluvial 0.312082 / 0.215719 / 4,143 / 156,093.613; river 0.286692 / 0.314930 / 9,572 / 224,609.914; coastal 0.063576 / 0.091893 / 0 / 51,790.734; heat 0.108673 / 0.187858 / 2,618 / 115,155.239.

These are deterministic exercise outputs. Affected resident-equivalent and system pressure are post-network snapshots; person-hours are cumulative event-attributable weighted local pre-network shortfall versus a matched no-event baseline. None is an observation, customer count, casualty estimate, forecast or operator promise.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, baseline, causal-ledger, allocation, reconciliation and monotonic-burden contracts pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1742 pnpm audit:model passes two tests on current code across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services.
Every intensity-zero run has zero event severity, affected resident-equivalent and event-attributable person-hours; repeated output, causal sums, counterfactuals and web/core preset parity pass.

All 46 rows reconcile exactly to 38,836 residents; all service demand/delivery totals reconcile, local hazard is service-layer invariant, person-hours are monotonic and declared logical route ceilings hold.
Passing arithmetic and deterministic contracts does not calibrate local hazards, populations, topology, services, response or recovery.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A shared cross-hazard neighbourhood seed and failed Holterberg source-containment test invalidate local spatial interpretation.
notes: At T+24 all eight nonzero single-hazard families with non-tied local detail share exactly the same top five: Hagslagen, De Beuseberg, Dannenberg, Buurtschap Look and Veeneslagen Oost. Earthquake is a zero tie; compound saturates several areas at one.

The ordering cannot simultaneously represent wind/tree exposure, 70 mm rain/sewer/rail-underpass flow, Regge/Schipbeek catchments, urban heat, snow/ice, a cyber target, Holterberg fire/smoke and indirect coastal effects.

A controlled source inside BRT mixed forest and BU17420303 De Holterberg produces direct fire 0.616925, smoke 0.513153 and severity 0.592570 from T+12 to T+36, but its neighbourhood ranks 13/46 while Hagslagen leads.

The canonical remote fire gives zero direct fire but smoke 0.352651 and drought 0.586914 at T+24. Its synthetic origin may be displayed only with explicit distance, evidence class and uncertainty; it does not test the locally material Holterberg incident.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight balances are inspectable, but exact service values are disconnected from GM1742's multi-owner water chain, utilities, routes, care and supplies.
notes: At river T+24 availability is power 61.42%, water 60.72%, drainage 46.76%, gas 77.96%, telecom 57.38%, mobility 85.96%, facilities 68.62% and supply 89.82%. No cited operator validates those values, reserves, dependencies or repair paths.

HWH points and the adopted programme identify sewer, surface-water and wastewater classes across three water boards, while Vitens drinking water is distinct. They do not provide complete catchment/pipe connectivity, flows, setpoints, power/backup or incident state.

NWB is correctly constrained to mobility and assumed road logistics. NBNL planning, Enexis public pages, RDI antennas, DUO schools, ProRail and GTFS do not support electricity/gas feeders, telecom backhaul, physical facility dependencies or live delivery.

No safe complete public source supplies drinking-water, electricity, gas, telecom, care, food/medicine, crew, stock or restoration topology. Preserve a privacy-safe aggregate synthetic fallback with explicit uncertainty and operator override.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes are visible, but unsupported local pathway, target, occupancy and operating dimensions are not declared by the precise outputs.
notes: River labels spatialEvidence derived-screening while emitting exact persistent GM1742 depth and severity without a named Regge/Schipbeek/Soestwetering boundary condition, rainfall, soil/groundwater state, catchment, control, footprint, arrival or recession.

Compound reports unsupportedDimensions=[] while its storm/pluvial/cyber components lack event-valid weather, tunnel/catchment, target, utility, occupancy and response support. Empty unsupported dimensions is materially misleading.

Current drought, Enexis or road pages; 2023–2027 policy; annual registers; BRT 2024 land use; 2025 planning; and synthetic checkpoints have different evidence and time classes and must never be fused.

Cyber requires a selected target/scope; earthquake requires an event/ground-motion method; fire requires ignition/perimeter/weather; winter/storm require event-valid fields. Missing inputs remain Unknown, not inferred local precision.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound states and all recovery curves lack accountable actions, resources, prerequisites, inspections and operator evidence.
notes: River depth/severity is 0.914835/0.286692 from T+12 through T+72. Pressure/affected/person-hours increase from 0.314930/9,572/224,609.914 at T+24 to 0.336796/10,768/928,344.129 at T+72 without a hydrologic or action state.

River T+72 remains power 0.614181, water 0.607235, drainage 0.467577, gas 0.779624, telecom 0.573794, mobility 0.859638, facilities 0.530013 and supply 0.898170. Those plateaus are not operator commitments.

Compound T+72 is severity 0.428918, pressure 0.535838, affected 21,658 and person-hours 1,486,582.741; all eight service availabilities freeze from T+48 despite changing hazard. No crew, fuel, spares, water, route or decision explains it.

A first-72-hour ledger must record owner, authority, target, status, resource, prerequisite, route/tunnel/rail access, start/end, confidence and blocking reason. Reopening requires inspection; restoration requires operator confirmation; seventy-two hours is a preparedness horizon, not a recovery deadline.

findings.summary: Generated identity, regional membership, settlements and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 confirms GM1742, Rijssen-Holten, Overijssel, 38,836 residents, 46 neighbourhoods/ten districts, two active BAG places and ten BRT settlements; the full contract confirms centre containment and exact deterministic reconciliation.
findings.action: Retain edition, retrieval, rounding and source-purpose metadata. Continue testing municipality, neighbourhood, BAG and BRT identity independently rather than treating labels as operational zones.

findings.summary: Current notices, plans, registers, NoData and zero matches are not sufficiently gated from operational claims.
findings.evidence: E01, E04, E06 and E07 expose null fields, no local observations, a time-bounded current street closure, a live 'none known' utility page, annual registers and planning samples. None alters the simulation, yet exact outputs do not enumerate missing dimensions; compound even reports unsupportedDimensions=[].
findings.action: Show source class, publisher, retrieved/observed/issued/valid/expiry time, coverage, licence, affectsSimulation and freshness beside every layer/output. Render Unknown/NoData distinctly from official zero, no matching record, expired, planned, simulated and safe; fail closed in exports.

findings.summary: A national named-major-river screen creates unsupported persistent direct inundation in Rijssen-Holten.
findings.evidence: E02 says Twente has no primary defences and only locally limited, short-lived Regge/Dinkel overflow during heavy/prolonged rain. The focused run instead fixes a 0.914835 m value and severity 0.286692 from T+12–72, reaching 10,768 affected resident-equivalents without selecting the Regge, Schipbeek, Soestwetering, a hydrograph, footprint or control state.
findings.action: Suppress direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel precision for GM1742 while retaining indirect regional effects as Unknown. Add separately governed Regge, Schipbeek/Soestwetering and pluvial events only from authority-reviewed hydraulic/stress-test inputs with rainfall/hydrograph, controls, arrival/recession, resolution, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial standing water omits the documented sewer, groundwater, surface-water and rail-underpass pathways.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the model emits 0.432113 m flood and 4,143 affected resident-equivalents. E03 instead documents infiltration/wadis/blue arteries/separation, a 70 mm/hour new-system goal and heavy-rain failure at three named rail underpasses that impairs north-south traffic and platform access; E04 and E07 add high-sand/groundwater and three-board control context.
findings.action: Drive pluvial impact from duration-specific KNMI forcing, AHN flow/low points, soil/groundwater, current municipal sewer/overflow/pump/catchment data and water-board receiving levels. Model the three underpasses and station access explicitly; a 70 mm/hour goal is not proof of achieved protection.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active single-hazard families reuse one exact neighbourhood priority order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Hagslagen, De Beuseberg, Dannenberg, Buurtschap Look and Veeneslagen Oost first through fifth, despite E02–E05 establishing different wind, water, heat, cyber and fire mechanisms.
findings.action: Remove the shared seeded multiplier from physical hazard rank. Until independent versioned surfaces exist, render municipality amplitude uniformly or mark neighbourhood hazard unresolved; then test rank diversity, source containment and source-specific spatial provenance per hazard.

findings.summary: A controlled ignition inside Holterberg mixed forest does not prioritize its containing neighbourhood.
findings.evidence: E05 verifies [6.41620728068325,52.29244865158755] inside BRT 2024 mixed forest and BU17420303 De Holterberg. T+12–36 direct fire is 0.616925 and smoke 0.513153, yet De Holterberg ranks 13/46 while Hagslagen leads; the canonical remote source produces no direct flame locally.
findings.action: Create a governed Holterberg exercise using an explicit authority ignition/perimeter, BRT/BBK fuels, current drought and KNMI wind, barriers, paths/escape routes, visitors, firefighting-water and suppression state. Require source-neighbourhood priority unless an auditable spread model explains otherwise.

findings.summary: The graph omits the municipality's internal rail-underpass, station-access, rail and current-road dependencies.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies A1/rail and dangerous-goods importance; E03 says three underpasses fill and the station platform becomes inaccessible; E06 shows eight boundary-road proxies plus stations/stops but no internal tunnel objects, and a valid 2–4 September municipal closure not consumed by the model.
findings.action: Add source-stable internal corridor/tunnel/station connectors with mode-specific state, owner, geometry, detours, emergency priority, issue/valid/expiry and inspection/reopening status. Ingest municipal/NDW/RWS/ProRail current notices where licences permit; absence stays Unknown and shared A1 edges stay non-additive.

findings.summary: Exact water, power, gas and telecom trajectories lack physical topology and operator restoration evidence.
findings.evidence: E07 exposes 82 partial water points, one electricity planning sample and 74 antenna records but no complete connectivity/state. River T+24 nevertheless reports exact availability from drainage 46.76% to supply 89.82%; Enexis congestion or 'none known' pages and NBNL queues do not validate an outage curve.
findings.action: Use authorised privacy/security-safe aggregate service zones, dependency interfaces, live incident state, backup bands and restoration estimates from municipality, water boards, Vitens, Enexis/gas and telecom operators. Until then retain explicit synthetic ranges/Unknown and never infer topology from register points.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits Holterberg visitors, commuters, workers, pupils, passengers, care clients and external acute-care demand.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies campsites/day visitors and evacuation factors; E06 has two stations and 152 stop areas; E07 has 30 schools and no internal covered SEH; E08 places acute hospitals outside GM1742 and identifies home-care/device vulnerability. None feeds a timestamped occupancy or reachable destination.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe scenario-time occupancy ranges and confidence for recreation, accommodation, work, education, transit, care and home medical dependence. Bind external hospital/reception destinations to acceptance, staffing, backup and current accessible road/rail routes; never promote schools or registers to shelters.

findings.summary: Weather, heat/drought, winter, cyber, seismic and coastal-indirect precision lacks local event fields and support boundaries.
findings.evidence: E02 and E04 support plausible wind, extreme rain, heat/drought, winter disruption, cyber and low-probability seismic context, but no event is selected. Coastal direct depth is correctly zero for the narrow source while nonzero wind/service pressure persists; the Groningen earthquake has zero T+24 ground motion but a synthetic 0.069046 peak; cyber has no target.
findings.action: Require valid KNMI fields for storm/heat/winter, named drought/water states, a declared cyber target/scope, and selected KNMI seismic origin plus ground-motion/site response. Keep coastal direct water zero for this source while labelling indirect supply effects separately and withholding unsupported exactness.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration, plateaus and recovery are not tied to accountable actions, resources or access prerequisites.
findings.evidence: River depth is fixed T+12–72 and person-hours rise to 928,344.129; compound freezes all services at T+48–72 while 21,658 remain affected and person-hours reach 1,486,582.741. E02, E03, E06 and E08 require warning, tunnel/route decisions, visitor/care actions, water, external care, backup and supplies, none of which appears in the ledger.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, fire prediction, road/rail decision, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and resident-based. They exclude incident-time visitors, overnight guests, commuters, pupils, patients, staff, road/rail passengers, responders and displaced people; no timestamped occupancy is consumed.

Generalized polygons and label points cannot resolve Regge, Schipbeek or Soestwetering catchments, terrain flow, sewer/groundwater systems, three rail underpasses, combustible vegetation, smoke or utility/service zones.

The Twente profile supports suppressing generic named-major-river direct precision, not declaring Rijssen-Holten flood-safe. Local river, brook, pluvial, groundwater, sewer, tunnel and indirect IJssel effects remain unresolved until an event is governed.
The 70 mm/hour target applies to new-system design and planned adaptation; it is not achieved protection, a live capacity test or proof that existing districts/tunnels remain passable.

Vechtstromen's current drought page is regional and time-sensitive. Its statements and lifted restrictions cannot be projected through the synthetic T+72 clock or across Rijn en IJssel/WDOD territory.

HWH coverage is partial and provider-dependent; 74/82 assets lack capacity and five lack a named manager. Registered/realised points do not establish connectivity, compatible capacity, current operation, power, controls or recovery.

BRT mixed forest is dated land-cover eligibility, not current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, visitors, access, firefighting water, crews or suppression. The controlled source is synthetic.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS, municipal notices and NDW have different coverage and time semantics. They do not establish scenario-time A1, rail, tunnel, station, bus, detour or emergency-route capacity, passengers, priority or restoration.
The 2–4 September road notice is current only inside its stated validity and expected reopening window. It must expire or be superseded; absence of a matching feed record is not an all-clear.

RIVM's zero internal acute-care respondent locations does not erase local care or demand. External hospital acceptance, ambulance travel, staffing, beds, diversion, backup, fuel and supplies remain Unknown.

One NBNL postcode sample, grid-congestion material, Enexis live place page, RDI antennas and DUO schools do not establish customer connectivity, live load/outage, coverage/backhaul, occupancy, shelter role, reserve or repair.

Complete physical power, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply and emergency-resource topology, live state, backup, stock, crew and restoration data may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.
Zero local KNMI station/seismic, Waterinfo, PM2.5 or acute-care matches are bounded dataset outcomes, never zero weather, seismic hazard, surface/ground water, smoke or care need.

Exact local hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic/derived until critical/high findings are corrected and responsible authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 remain outside scope.
